newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Amnesty calls for safeguards for Rwandan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty calls for safeguards for Rwandan refugees.

text.p: The head of the human rights group Amnesty International warned on Tuesday that the return of Rwandan refugees from Zaire could lead to an escalation of cases of miscarriages of justice.
"We continue to receive information about arbitrary arrests...and prisoners continue to die in overcrowded prisons," Amnesty International Secretary General Pierre Sane told a news conference.

Sane said he met senior Rwandan government ministers and police officers last week, receiving assurances refugees would not be arrested on suspicion of involvement in Rwanda's 1994 genocide without firm evidence. The government said it was also taking steps to ease prison overcrowding.

Around one million people, mainly members of Rwanda's minority Tutsi ethnic group, died at the hands of militias led by Rwanda's Hutu majority in the bloody conclusion of a civil war in 1994 that ended with Tutsi rebels winning power.

Hundreds of thousands of Hutus fled, fearing reprisals, to Zaire, from where they are now returning after the outbreak last month of related ethnic clashes around the camps where they had been based for the last two years.
Sane called for the number of United Nations observers in Rwanda, monitoring the return of refugees to their towns of origin, to be increased.
Sane was responding to a question from a journalist at a news conference called to present Amnesty International's latest report on the human rights situation in Algeria.
